findings: ST-Net fine-tunes an ImageNet DenseNet-121 on 224 by 224 pixel patches to predict the log normalised expression of the 250 genes with the highest mean expression, on sections from 23 breast cancer patients. Every result is leave-one-patient-out, training on 22 patients. The paper does not study how accuracy depends on the number of training patients; the authors only say they chose the smallest DenseNet because training data were limited.
numbers: 23 patients, training on 22 per fold. RMSE 0.31 on log expression. 102 of 250 genes correlate positively in 20 or more of the 23 patients (FDR 0.05). External 10x data: 207 of 234 genes positive, mean Pearson 0.33. GNAS median correlation 0.34, FASN 0.31 (Table 1).
locations: Main text, Results paragraphs 1 to 4; Table 1; Methods (model and training).
caveats: No learning curve, so Q1 and Q2 gain no scaling evidence from this paper. Supplement not opened. Version (accepted manuscript or typeset) not determined; the PDF carries the journal layout.

findings: Gives an upper bound on the power of any test that detects whether one individual is in a pool from released allele frequencies, through the likelihood ratio test. For m independent common SNPs and a pool of n individuals, z_alpha + z_(1-beta) is approximately sqrt(m/n), so the number of statistics that can be released safely grows linearly in n. Applied to C1 by analogy only: a center that releases about 1.26 million sums for tens of thousands of spots has m/n far above one, so the bound gives no protection, which motivates V3's noise.
numbers: Equation (1), valid for n above 100 and minor allele frequency above 0.05. Simulation n = 1,000, m = 1,000 and 10,000. WTCCC 2,937 individuals, 33,138 SNPs after prefiltering, pool of 1,000: power below 0.95 at false-positive rate 1e-3 and below 0.5 at 1e-6.
locations: Main text (Brief Communication), equation (1) and Figure 1.
caveats: The bound is for independent binary genotype summaries, not continuous embedding cross-products; the analogy to C1 is the session's, not the paper's. Supplementary Note with the derivation not opened.

full_text_source: PDF supplied by Nicolas, ~/hest-1k/fedlearn_papers/requested/Proportionally_Fair_Hospital_Collaborations_in_Federated_Learning_of_Histopathology_Images.pdf; read 14 October
findings: Proposes Prop-FFL, a FedSGD variant whose server objective adds a proportional-fairness term, and tests it on TCGA kidney subtyping (4 hospitals, patch level) and lung LUAD against LUSC (6 hospitals, slide level, attention MIL), both on frozen ImageNet DenseNet-121 features of length 1,024. Per-hospital test accuracy under plain FedSGD varies widely across hospitals, and the fairness objective narrows the spread mainly by raising the worst hospital. No centralised (pooled) arm is reported in the per-hospital tables.
numbers: Table IV kidney, FedSGD per hospital 71.23, 72.01, 66.87, 82.41 (variance 32.54); q-FedSGD variance 11.22; Prop-FFL 78.84, 77.12, 76.21, 84.36 (variance 10.00). Table V lung, FedSGD 66.22, 58.06, 50.14, 74.19, 71.20, 40.13 (variance 143.54); q-FedSGD variance 53.89; Prop-FFL 72.23, 76.81, 74.57, 74.50, 76.44, 60.81 (variance 29.84). Means over five runs. Default lambda 0.6.
locations: Section IV-A (datasets), IV-C, Tables IV and V (read from the page image), Figures 9 and 10.
caveats: Tables IV and V are images in the PDF; their values were read from the page image (journal page 1990) and checked a second time against it. Accuracies are percentages. Training stopped after 300 rounds on the histopathology sets. Appendix B (FedAvg) not read in detail.
